transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-21
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Ethan Park (Redwood SRE), Maria Lopez (Aperture CTO), Kevin Zhang (Aperture SRE), Sara Kim (Aperture PM)

Summary:
Quick follow-up on the reliability incident that hit the POC earlier this week (timeouts, elevated 5xxs, rate-limiting behavior). SE presented initial RCA, discussed mitigation (retry/backoff, rate-limit tuning, autoscaler knobs), and agreed on next steps: share full logs, run targeted benchmark with revised retry/backoff, consider temporary Dedicated burst for peak window.

Topics:
- Incident timeline and cause hypothesis
- Retry/Backoff and client-side rate limit config
- Autoscaler quota and provisioning delays
- Fallbacks: model variant and regional routing
- Security/observability artifacts requested (audit logs, KMS key usage)

Action items (recap in call): see action_items field above for owners/due dates.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: ok hey everyone thanks for hopping on, um this is the weekly POC sync, main agenda is to follow up on the incident from Tuesday, go over root cause, and get next steps. Maria, Kevin, thanks for making time.
[00:20] Maria: yeah thanks Jordan, anxious to understand what happened, we had pretty bad user impact in the 10:00-10:30am window, lots of timeouts reported.
[00:30] Kevin: we saw a bunch of 5xxs and then client-side retries started piling up which made it worse, kind of a retry storm, so we want to avoid that pattern going forward.
[00:40] Priya: right, initial look from our side - we correlate increased tail latency on the Redwood runtime with a brief autoscaler delay provisioning new workers for the burst, and the customer client library defaults were aggressive for retries. also noticed a couple of rate-limit 429 spikes from the gateway.
[01:05] Ethan: and to add, there were a handful of instances where the KV cache miss rate spiked because the prefix caching wasn't warming for certain seq lengths, which increased computation per request for a few minutes.
[01:30] Maria: hmm KV cache warming, can you unpack that a bit?
[01:36] Priya: sure, so we saw a workload shift - longer context requests hit that minute where the cache was cold; the runtime then had to re-compute embeddings for prefixes, leading to higher per-token latency and some CPU/GPU scheduling delays. transcription might show 'KV cash' in some logs, sorry for the typo, it's 'KV cache'.
[02:05] Sara: are these things that would have been caught by the canary rollout? we thought we had a canary configured for traffic ramp.
[02:12] Jordan: yeah good question - we did a canary but the spike came from a short external event (integration job) that didn't hit canary population; plus the autoscaler policy was set to a conservative scale-up cooldown which delayed node provisioning.
[02:35] Kevin: also quota limits, our cloud account hit a per-region GPU quota briefly which blocked rapid provisioning, that's on our side but impacted response time.
[02:48] Priya: thanks for calling that out, Kevin. So short-term mitigations we discussed: tune client retries to use exponential backoff with jitter, cap concurrent in-flight requests per client to avoid retry storms, adjust autoscaler aggressive mode for the pilot windows, and optionally bump to a small Dedicated burst for the high-traffic window.
[03:10] Maria: can you send a recommended config for retries? we have a couple services with default retry 3x immediate which obviously made things worse.
[03:16] Priya: absolutely - recommended: 1-2 retries max, initial backoff 200-500ms, exponential multiplier 2, max backoff 5s, add jitter. We'll send a sample client config we used in other pilots.
[03:36] Jordan: I'll also note that we observed gateway 429s before the bulk of 5xxs - seems the frontend rate limiter kicked in as requests surged, then clients retried, and that cascaded. We recommend implementing client-side throttling to smooth bursts.
[03:55] Sara: ok makes sense. From a timeline perspective we need this fixed for the next customer demo on 2026-05-28. Is that feasible?
[04:03] Ethan: yes, with the mitigations we can get SLOs back for that window, provided we get the sample payloads and agree on retry settings; also we'll run an in-prod-ish benchmark (same seq lengths, same concurrency) to validate.
[04:20] Kevin: one ask - can you share the incident logs and any stack traces? we'll correlate with our side.
[04:25] Priya: yes, SE will share incident RCA and a log bundle link (redacted for PII). link posted in chat: https://redwood.internal/incident/apt-4829 (note: internal link; we'll provide sanitized copy).
[04:45] Maria: also for auditing we need to confirm KMS usage and whether any customer data was logged or persisted.
[04:52] Jordan: short answer: no customer PII was persisted beyond ephemeral logs; we will include a KMS usage statement in the RCA, and the security pack (SOC2 docs) is already in your shared folder.
[05:05] Sara: one more technical Q - is there an easy way to force fallback to a smaller model variant when latency spikes? to keep errors low.
[05:12] Priya: yes, you can set an automated routing policy to fallback to a lower-cost model variant or to another region; we showed that in the demo last week. small note: sometimes model output quality shifts but for error mitigation it's a valid lever.
[05:35] Kevin: worth noting too that some 5xxs were internal runtime OOMs when the sequence length exploded; recommendation was to enforce max context trims at the client or compress the prompt.
[05:50] Jordan: right, we flagged a few requests with >12k tokens which pushed the runtime. we'll include a prompt sanitizer example in the repo.
[06:10] Maria: ok good. on the autoscaler side, do we need to change cloud quotas now or just increase cooldown aggressiveness?
[06:18] Kevin: we'll request quota bump but it takes a little time - for immediate relief we'll change the policy to faster scale-up and pre-warm a small standby pool during demo windows.
[06:33] Priya: we'll provide the autoscaler policy diff and suggested standby pool size.
[06:40] Sara: what about observability - can you add more detailed traces to see which stage is slow (gateway vs runtime vs model)?
[06:48] Ethan: yes we can enhance tracing for the pilot: per-request trace, token-level timings, and correlation IDs. that will help pinpoint hotspots.
[07:02] Maria: ok what's the plan for validating fixes? can we run a replay of the failed traffic?
[07:08] Priya: Kevin to share sample failed payloads and timestamps; we'll replay them on a staging harness and then run the in-prod benchmark with the client retry config.
[07:20] Kevin: I'll assemble payloads and put them in the shared drive, target 2026-05-23.
[07:26] Jordan: great. timeline recap: Priya sends RCA and config by 05-22, Kevin shares payloads by 05-23, then we run a benchmark and report back in the next weekly sync or earlier if needed.
[07:39] Sara: any impact on pilot budget if we spin up Dedicated burst? curious about cost.
[07:45] Jordan: we'll send a short note with Dedicated burst pricing and temporary uplift estimates; for the short demo window it's usually small but we'll quantify.
[07:54] Maria: also please include any mitigations we can do from our side to avoid causing spikes - better client throttling, scheduled background jobs outside demo windows, etc.
[08:05] Priya: yes, we'll include a runbook with best-practices: client-side throttles, max context limits, backoff config, and how to enable model fallback policies.
[08:18] Ethan: quick aside - we detected a small number of gateway mis-parses where product names were transcribed differently in the logs; it's low priority but we fixed the logging mapping.
[08:30] Kevin: thanks. do you have a tentative date for the in-prod benchmark?
[08:34] Priya: aiming for the week of 05-25, depending on payloads and quota.
[08:40] Jordan: ok, anything else?
[08:42] Maria: no, thanks everyone. appreciate the quick turnaround.
[08:46] Jordan: thanks all - recap of next steps in chat and we'll send the RCA and configs.
